exercise1.prompt: Use print(), len() and type() on the string "Python"

cases.name: prints the length of the string
prints the type of the string
cases.describe: what type() says about a string

cases.name: the answers come from the built-in functions, not from typing them out
cases.describe: print(), len() and type() all called in your code

exercise1.hint: The two answers are things Python can work out for you. If either number or word is typed into your code as a literal, the built-in function that produces it is missing.

questions.explain: len counts the characters. "Python" has six of them, and the count is a number rather than the word itself.

questions.prompt: What is the main reason to put repeated code in a function?
choices: It makes the program run faster
It means the steps are written once and can be run as often as you like
Python requires every program to have one
It stops the program from crashing
questions.explain: A function names a block of steps so they can be run again by name. Writing them once is what makes a change to them a change in one place.

questions.prompt: Which of these are functions Python gives you without any import?
questions.explain: print, len and type are built-in functions. def is a keyword: it is how you write a function of your own, not a function you call.

questions.prompt: Match each built-in function to what it does.
right: shows a value on the screen
says what kind of value something is
questions.explain: print shows a value, len measures one, and type describes one. Only print puts anything on the screen; the other two hand a value back for you to use.

questions.prompt: Fill in the built-in function that reports how many characters are in a string: ___("Python")
questions.explain: len is the built-in that measures the size of a string, a list or any other collection.
